description.narrative:
The Masarouna programme implements two main pathways of change:
1: Lobby and advocacy with young people for their SRHR The first pathway promotes greater accountability of governments to adhere to international SRHR standards, human rights frameworksand agreements; promotes young people’s active and meaningful involvement in policy agenda-setting and decision-making; and increases public awareness on SRHR, including through media engagement, aiming to create new narratives on SRHR.
2: Strengthening civil society and reinventing civic space A strong civil society can be a mobilizer, an amplifier of voices and a watchdog. With strengthened capacities,CSOs can create a sense of urgency around SRHR to push for sustainable change. CSOs need the spaceto play this political role, which Masarouna aims to reinvent by promoting the political activation and participation of young people and creating and strengthening alternative civic spaces, both online and offline. Working online allows for reaching young people at scale by circumventing gatekeepersand mitigating risks around censorship.
Under this project, and through its theory of change, Oxfam has committed to continue supporting 6 organizations national level- Palestinian human and women's rights organizations. Believing that driving positive impact can be achieved through building national partnerships that focuses on creating spaces for the active engagement of right holders and working together towards holding key stakeholders accountable todrive structural change. Oxfam will continue facilitating strengthening partners capacities, through supporting the organizational and financial capacities of partners throughout the course of the project implementation. Likewise, Oxfam will work towardsoffering capacity building opportunities to partners in key areas that will increase the quality of implementation by linking with national and International expertise (through linking with HQ staff) to build their capacities in influencing skills, focusing on International Influencing specifically on the UN Influencing mechanisms, youth active citizenship, women transformative leadership, civic space. Likewise, Oxfam will work on linking the work of partners to international level, making use of international events, fora and mechanisms to raise young people and partners voices on SRHR rights. Similarly, Oxfam will facilitate wider alliances through linking with its wide network of partners and coalitions and through theimplementation of internationaladvocacy trips to increase CSOs influence on national and international decision makers by linking and building local regional and international alliances for gender sensitive peace and security.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.

description.narrative: KI-13 # Women led CSOs/ movements supported by Masarouna to strengthen their civic space influencing capacity

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey was conducted in 2021, screening partners' capacities in reclaiming civic space and strengthening partnerships. Most partners expressed a need for capacity strengthening in the following areas: widening (digital) civic space for young people working on SHRH; civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, partners and people we work with; protection in digital space; and strengthening/broadening partnerships. Most organisations stated already having a strong capacity in shaping positive narratives. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic.) In the CATool survey conducted in 2022, both new women led partners expressed an interest to increase their capacityon understanding and navigating (offline and online) civic space for young people working on SRHR. One new partner also expressed an interest to increase their capacity on civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, partners and people we work with; protection in digital space; health and wellbeing; perception by & relation with constituency; and strengthening/broadening partnerships (movements & coalitions). Between them, the new partners expressed having experience in supporting others on healthand wellbeing; strengthening/broadening partnerships (movements & coalitions); digital security, digital appearance, crisis management, hate speech, reputation and smear campaigns.

In relation civic space influencing, two women led partners of the Oxfam Country Office and RNW Media reported an increased capacity since joining the programme. One partner reported an increased capacity on Understanding and navigating civic space, and Protection in digital space. The second partner reported an increased capacity on civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff; protection in digital space; and health and wellbeing. Based on the criteria agreed on, both organisations realized an actual for KI-13 in 2022 against the target for 2022. However, one of these two CSOs is not counted in the quantitative actual for KI-13, as it was already counted as an actual under KI-6 (avoiding double-counting). Among the three other women led partner organisations of the Oxfam Country Office, two reported an increased capacity related to civic space influencing since joining the programme, however, based on the criteria agreed, these three organisations did not yet realize an actual for KI-13 in 2022 against the target for 2022. All five women led organisations expressed an interest to (further) increase their capacity on several capacities related to civic space influencing over the course of the programme Two new women led partners of RNW Media that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to civic space influencing over the course of the programme. (Source: CATool 2022)

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, one women-led organisation realized an actual for KI-13 in 2023. This organisation (a partner of both Oxfam and RNW Media) reported increased capacity on Protection in digital space; and Health and wellbeing in 2023, resulting in an actual for KI-13 in 2023 against a target in 2022. The actual for the partner organisation is not reported in IATI as it was already reported for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-13] in 2022.

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, one women-led organisation realized an actual for KI-13 in 2024. This partner of Oxfam reported increased capacity on Civic space risk mitigation and protection of staff; Health and wellbeing; and Strengthen/broaden partnerships, resulting in an actual in 2024. The actual for the partner organisation is not reported in IATI as it was already reported for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6] in 2023. Moreover, another reported increased capacity on Understanding and navigating civic space in 2024, however, based on the criteria agreed on the partner did not realise an actual in 2024 while worth mentioning that they already achieved an actual aganist KI-13 in 2022. Onthe other hand, 4 women led partners of Oxfam and RNW Media maintained their capacity during 2024, while one partner of Oxfam reported decreased capacity on Civic space risk mitigation and protection of staff and Protection in digital space.

A capacity building plan will be developed based on the three priorities for capacity building identified by Masarouna partners (safety and well-being, dialogue and consultation, and access to information and public voice). RNW Media will strengthen CSOs on several aspects regarding civic cpace influencing, including strengthening the digital rights knowledge of CSOs and movements. RNW Media will also provide capacity strengthening support on media campaigns for social change, which will enable CSOs to use media engagement for changing the civic space and build public awareness.

As a result of capacity strengthening provided by RNW Media, partners will improve their practices and policies in digital safety and security to be applied in their work on digital campaigning. The Oxfam Country Office will be working with the adolescents coalition on wellbeing and, following its national influencing strategy, it will open the space for youth and partners for dialogue and consultation with stakeholders and relevant line ministries to call for change. Additionally, Oxfam is currently in the process of assessing existing digital spaces to upgrade them to be me more accessible to young women with disabilities needs to access information on SRHR.

description.narrative: KI-12 # Women led CSOs/ movements supported by Masarouna to strengthen their organizational capacities

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey was conducted in 2021, screening partners' organizational capacities and capacities on cross-cutting themes. Capacity strengthening priorities most often indentified by partners are feminist MEAL, safeguarding (response), staff health & care and fundraising. Most partners indicated to already have strong capacity on safeguarding (prevention); project management; project financial management; SRHR foundational knowledge; youth engagement practices; feminist approach to SRHR and SRHR influencing; gender & power analysis; mainstreaming gender justice and social inclusion; transformative leadership; and analyzing & integrating conflict sensitivity. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic). In the CATool survey conducted in 2022, both new women led partners expressed an interest in increasing their capacity on Feminist MEAL. One new partner also expressed an interest to increase their capacity on SRHR; youth engagement practices; feminist approaches to SRHR influencing; gender and power analysis; mainstreaming gender and social exclusion; transformative leadership; working with specific target groups relevant to the program; analyzing and integrating conflict sensitivity; safeguarding (prevention & response); project (financial) management; and fundraising. Between them, the new partners indicated to have experience in supporting others on youth engagement practices; working with specific target groups relevant to the program; and project (financial) management.

In relation to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, two women-led Oxfam partners realized an actual for KI-12 in 2023. The first partner reported increased capacity on Youth engagement practices; Mainstream gender justice and social exclusion; Transformative leadership; Safeguarding, prevention; and Safeguarding, response, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2022. The second partner reported increased capacity on SRHR Foundational knowledge; Youthengagement practices; Working with specific target groups; Safeguarding: response; and Project Management in 2022, and on Safeguarding: prevention; Project financial management; and Fundraising in 2023, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2022. The actuals for both partners for KI-12 in 2023 are not reported in IATI as actuals were already reported for them in IATI for KI-6 and KI-12 respectively in 2022.

In relation to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity, the first partner reported increased capacity on Analyse and integrate conflict sensitivity; Mainstream gender justice and social exclusion; Transformative leadership; and Safeguarding: responding to cases of inappropriate behaviour in 2024. The second partner reported increased capacity on Analyse and integrate conflict sensitivity; Feminist MEAL; Safeguarding: prevention of inappropriate behaviour; and Safeguarding: responding to cases of inappropriate behaviour in 2024. And the third partner reported increased capacity on (SRHR) foundational knowledge; Youth engagement practices; Feminist approaches to SRHR influencing; Gender and power analysis; Transformative leadership; and Working with specific target groups in 2024. Moreover, the fourth partner reported increased capacity on Fundraising in 2024. Based on the criteria agreed on, none of the aforementioned partners achieved an actual on KI-12. Additionally, the fifth partner reported decreased capacity on 12 capacity areas in 2024 due to the conflict and the unability to implement the programme.

In relation to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity, two women led partners of the Oxfam Country Office reported an increased capacity since joining the programme. One partner reported an increased capacity on SRHR foundational knowledge, Youth engagement practices, Working with specific target groups relevant to the program, Feminist MEAL, and Safeguarding: prevention. The second partner reported an increased capacity on SRHR foundational knowledge, Youth engagement practices, Working with specific target groups relevant to the program, Safeguarding: responding to cases of inappropriate behaviour, and Project management since joining the programme. Based on the criteria agreed on, both organisations realized an actual for KI-6 in 2022 against the target for 2022. However, one of these two CSOs is not counted in the quantitative actual for KI-12, as it was already counted as an actual under KI-6 (avoiding double-counting). The three other women-led organisations, partners of Oxfam and RNW Media also reported an increased capacity since joining the programme, however, based on the criteria agreed on they did not realize an actual for KI-12 in 2022 against the target for 2022. Planned activities for capacity strengthening were either postponed to 2023 or did not yet result in an actual in 2022. All five women led organisations expressed an interest to (further) increase their capacity on several capacities related to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity over the course of the programme. Two new women led partners of RNW Media that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity over the course of the programme. (Source: CATool 2022)

Capacity strengthening in relation to organizational capacities and capacities on cross-cutting themes will focus on the needs as expressed by respective organisations involved in Masarouna. These include capacity strengthening on feminist MEAL, safeguarding (response), staff health & care, fundraising, and youth engagement practices. As a result of close collaboration with RNW Media, the women led partner will have strengthened capacities on PMEAL and finance and project management. RNW Media will support masterclasses on the use of online data collection, analysis and visualisation to partners. In addition, being a member of RNW Media's network, the partner will benefit from network members expertise, be hired as technical experts and/or mutual strengthening of their organizational capacities to implement programmes.

As a result of continuous support from RNW Media, partners will improve their safeguarding policies and practices; as well as strengthen their organisational capacities in project management and financial management through continuous feedback and support during the implementation course. Hired as technical experts and/or mutual strengthening of their organizational capacities to implement programmes. The Capacity Assessment Tool (CATool) was carried out in 2022 and Oxfam has developed organizational capacity building plans for its project partners.

As a result of continuous support from RNW Media and local organization partners will improve their safeguarding policies and practicies; as well as strengthen their organisational capacities in project management through continuous feedback and support during the implementation course. In addition, RNW Media partner is taking part in the digital transformation trajectory of RNW Media to identify improvements points to strengthen their organisational and technical capacities related to digital reach and engagement. Along with the existing Oxfam Masarouna partners, women-led and young women-led organizations through the NGO coalition will engage in organisational capacity strengthening activities. (The new women led coalition partner is not included inthe target for KI-12/2024 in IATI to avoid double counting with the target reported for this organisation for KI-6 for 2024.)

description.narrative: KI-6 # Women led CSOs/movements capacitated by Masarouna to advocate for safe and adequate SRHR information and services for diverse young people

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey was conducted in 2021, screening seven different capacities under the topic of influencing and awareness raising on SRHR for young people. These are: developing an influencing strategy, youth-led influencing, lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, public campaigning, digital campaigning, working with traditional media, and influencing social norms. Digital campaigning stood out as the topic with the most needs. Lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, had a majority of organizations indicating a need, and public campaigning and influencing social norms each had about half indicating needs. With respect to lobby and/or advocacy, it was also mentioned that it is difficult to advocate for inclusive SRHR policies and that there is a need for alternatives to create inclusive SRHR policies, and hence for enhanced capacities for this. The topics for which most organizations involved in Masarouna indicated to already having a strong capacity and being eager to support others, are: working with traditional media; developing an influencing strategy; youth-led influencing and public campaigning. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic). In the CATool survey conducted in 2022, both new women led partners expressed an interest in increasing their capacity on developing an influencing strategy. One new partner also expressed a interest to increase their capacity on youth-led influencing; lobby and/oradvocacy on SRHR policies and practices; public campaigning; digital campaigning; working with traditional media; influencing social norms; digital presence; and digitalization of data. Between them, the new partners indicated to have experience in supporting others on, among other, influencing social norms, lobby and/or advocacy on SRHR policies and practices; public campaigning; digital campaigning and advocacy; digital presence.

In 2021, RNW Media started strengthening partners by providing capacity building in various aspects, however work done in this regard have not yet addressed capacity dimensions related to influencing on SRHR for diverse young people. 2021 was the first year of the program implementation and RNW Media prioritized efforts towards establishing partnerships with CSOs at country level. Capacitating partners, including on these capacity dimensions, will be continued in 2022.

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, five women-led organisations realized an actual for KI-6 in 2023. The 1st RNW Media partner reported increased capacity on Influencing strategies led by and with diverse young people; Digital campaigning; Working with traditional media; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2023. The 2nd RNW media partner reported increased capacity on Influencing strategies ledby and with diverse young people; Public campaigning; Influencing social norms; Working with traditional media; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2023. The 1st Oxfam partner reportedincreased capacity on Influencing strategies led by and with diverse young people; Digital campaigning; Influencing social norms; Working with traditional media; Developing an influencing strategy; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices in2023, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2022. The 2nd Oxfam partner reported increased capacity on Developing an influencing strategy; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2022. The 3rd Oxfam partner (3) reported increased capacity on Digital campaigning; Influencing social norms; Developing an influencing strategy; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a targetin 2022. The actuals of 3 partners are reported in IATI for 2023 as this is the first time they achieve an actual against 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6]. The actuals for the other two partners for KI-6 in 2023 are not reported in IATI as actuals were already reported for them for capacity strengthening KI-6 and KI-12 respectively in 2022.

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, two women-led organisations (one partner of Oxfam and one partner of RNW Media) realized an actual for KI-6 in 2024 as they reported increased capacity on Developing an influencing strategy; Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices; Public campaignin; and Digital campaigning. The actual is not reported in the quantitative info and in IATI to avoid double counting. Moreover, the partner of both Oxfam and RNW Media reportedincreased capacoty on Influencing social and social norms in 2024, however, that did not result in an actual for KI-6 in 2024. Additionally, a partner of RNW Media, and two partners of Oxfam maintained their capacity during the course of 2024, while the women led coalition (partner of Oxfam), have not yet reported their capacities. One Women led organisation (partner of Oxfam) reported decreased capacity on all capacity areas due to the conflict and the unability to implement the programme.

In relation to SRHR influencing with diverse young people, two women led partners of Oxfam Country Office reported an increased capacity since joining the programme. One partner reported an increased capacity on Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices, Public campaigning, Digital campaigning, Working with traditional media, and Influencing social norms. The second partner reported an increased capacity on Developing an influencing strategy, and Digital campaigning. Based on the criteria agreed on, both organisations realized an actual for KI-6 in 2022 against a target for 2022. Three other women led partners of Oxfam and RNW Media did not yet report an increased capacity related to SRHR influencing with diverse young people since joining the programme, and (hence) did not realize an actual for KI-6 in 2022 against a target for 2021 (1 organisation) and 2022 (2 organisations) . Planned activities for capacity strengthening were either postponed to 2023 or did not yet result in actuals in 2022. All five women led organisations expressed an interest to (further) increase their capacity on several capacities related to SHRH influencing with diverse young people over the course of the programme. Two new women led partners of RNW Media that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to SHRH influencing with diverse young people over the course of the programme. (Source: CATool 2022)

In 2021, as a result of the trainings offered by RNW Media, one of the women led organisatons is capacitated to create engaging SRHR content, involve and include media that can be engaged in advocacy and use of data for that advocacy.

In 2022, capacity strengthening in relation to influencing on SRHR for diverse young people will focus on the needs as expressed by respective organisations involved in Masarouna. These include capacity strengthening on digital campaigning, lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, public campaigning and influencing social norms. RNW Media will support one of the women led organisations on digital M&E, including a coaching trajectory focusing on which collecting data should be collected to serve youth needs for advocacy. As a result of this support, the organisation will have strenghtened capacity of using data for advocacy. Also, RNW Media will sensitise the organisation on the use of digital tools (such as the social listening tool) to inform,monitor and evaluate online campaigns and use this for advocacy purposes.

In 2023, as a result of capacity strengthening support from RNW Media, partners will improve their capacity in creating engaging SRHR content and establishing safe and adrquate digital campaigning on SRHR issues.

Oxfam Country Office will establish a partnership with a non-goverment organisations (NGO) coalition and the coalition will be engaged in influencing capacity strengthening activities. Among the +100 organisations that are NGO members, 12 women-led organisations will be directly engaged in Masarouna, and will be engaged in capacity strengthening activities, however. these will not participate in the CATool and are therefor not included in the quantitative target for this indicator.

As a result of capacity strengthening support from RNW Media, the women led partner will improve their capacity to monitor and collect data and use that data for SRHR advocacy (not included in the quantitative target to avoid double counting with previous years).

description.narrative: KI-16 # Women led CSOs/movements engaged in Masarouna

comment.narrative: Currently, Masarouna has 6 partners in the country. Interventions these organizations work on include lobby and/or advocacy, public campaigning, (social) media work, coalition building, awareness raising, research, capacity strengthening, and piloting projects. One women led partner is a national organization committed to social development, by addressing educational and counseling needs as they relate to SRHR. The organisation aspires to substantially raise community awareness to SRHR challenges and to create counseling and educational programs that will effectively contribute to individual and family development. By partnering and engaging with various community sectors, and by employing methods that reflect sensitivity to the socio-cultural context,the organisation hopes to effectively change the prevailing stereotypes and practices in society. In 2022 RNW Media contracted two new (women-led) partners in the country, one of them has more experience and capacity in digital safety, security, as well as digital rights, the other one is focusing on working with different vulnerable groups, such as youth, women, people with disabilities.

During the reporting period, the first women led partner of Oxfam focused on youth awareness, advocacy training, and initiatives, actively participating in referral mechanisms for GBV and SRH within its implementation areas in the country. The organization also conducted a needs assessment based on SRH and the ongoing conflict, helping to identify and address urgent health and protection concerns. The second partner of both Oxfam and RNW Media contributed by raising awareness and providing inclusive training on SRH for youth, their parents, and service providers. These efforts aimed to improve knowledge and access to essential SRH services, fostering a supportive environment for young people and their families. The third partner of Oxfam prioritized the inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (PWD) by ensuring their needs were met and enhancing accessibility to services and service providers. In collaboration with the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the fourth partner, the third partner worked to make the SRH strategy and emergency response plan more inclusive of PWD. The fourth partner of Oxfam collaborated with Oxfam to introduce a new curriculum at one University focused on preconception care and journalism education. The organization also played a keyrole in equipping safe spaces for SRH services. The fifth partner of Oxfam focused on monitoring and addressing restrictive laws and policies imposed. This partner worked to raise awareness among its members about self-protection and civic space rights,while also supporting youth through capacity-building initiatives to enhance their legal knowledge and advocacy skills. Throughout 2024, RNW Media continued collaborating with three women-led CSOs to advance SRHR in the country. These partnerships buildmutual capacity and bolster collective efforts within Masarouna.

In 2022, RNW Media engaged with two new women led CSOs, next to the one already engaged in 2021.
Oxfam Country Office continued engagement with five women-led CSOs in 2022. One of these has been successful in advocating for SRHR within their community. Despite being new in the field, the project has empowered them to play a leading role in promoting SRHR for women and girls with disabilities. In the upcoming year, this CSO will review the national SRHR strategy through a disability perspective.

In 2023, 5 women-led organisations continued being engaged in Masarouna in 2023 by the Oxfam country office. Additionally, the Oxfam country office partnered with a new women led coalition to enhance collaboration and joint efforts. In 2023, RNW Media continued and strengthened its collaboration with 3 women-led organisations in the country. (One of these partners is a partner of both RNW Media partner and Oxfam, hence not counted again in the actual).

The 5 women-led partner organisations have enhanced representing the SRHR agenda within their constituencies whereby partners assumed a leading role in establishing and leading on groups that include decision-makers and activists in the field of SRHR.
In 2021, RNW Media partnered with one of the women led organisations. The partnership contributes to reaching the Masarouna objectives and RNW Media objectives - in line with both partners' theories of change.

The Masarouna partnership starts and will evolve during the 1st year of implementation, where partners are working together and providing capacity support to each other. In 2021, RNW Media partners with a women-led organization. During the course of theproject, the partnership will be strengthened as the partners get to know each other and each other's strengths better. RNW Media would see the partnership evolve through collaboration, joint learning meetings, regular exchanges and possible introductionof new partners, which can be identified through the implementation and assessment of project activities.

The partnership is expected to be sustained throughout the project, and beyond, as the various partners have complementary roles to each other. It will also be explored whether humanr rights organizations can bring an added value to the partnership. RNWMedia has the ambition to expand its partner base with other types of organisations that can help reaching the Masarouna objectives. For example, research inistitutes to change social norms and provide evidence-based information for advocacy. Further, RNWMedia aims to explore new ways to promote learning and exchanging expertise among all partners and look for effective ways for partnership building, meeting structures and effective decision making.
The partnership between RNW Media and local organisations evolves through co-creation and mutual capacity building opportunities such as learning events and expertise exchange.

The partnerships between RNW Media and local organisations will be strengthened through further co-creation and mutual capacity strengthening opportunities such as learning events, resources and expertise exchange, as well as Community of Practice. Oxfam country office partnership with 5 women-led organisations is continued (among which one partner), and will establish a partnership with Non-goverment Organisations (NGO) coalition. Among the +100 organisations that are NGO members, 12 women-led organisations will be directly engaged in Masarouna.

The partnerships between RNW Media and three local women led organisations in the country will be strengthened through further co-creation and mutual capacity strengthening opportunities such as the learning events, regional trainings and the Community of Practice. In 2025, Oxfam in country will continue its partnership with four women-led organizations directly involved in the Masarouna project, including several women-led groups. Also, Oxfam will conduct research, in collaboration with four women ledpartners, on the impact of the conflict on women with disabilities in the country, which will contribute to a national influencing campaign. This research and the advocacy efforts will also involve communication and information exchange among women's groups. The sixth women led organisations is no longer Oxfam partner in 2025.

description.narrative: KI-16 # Youth led CSOs/movements engaged in Masarouna
KI-1a # Governmental policies blocked, adopted and/or improved to enable diverse young people to enjoy their SRHR

comment.narrative: Laws and regulations in general fail to protect women, girls and other marginalized groups. The legal framework further hinders young people's ability to exercise their SRHR rights. Applicable laws, for example, condone Gender Based Violence (GBV). Additionally, the outdated legal framework does not take into account the different needs of marginalized and vulnerable groups in present day times. GBV is a key concern. Child marriage is an increasing phenomenon, with 24% of children getting married beforethe age of 18; a negative coping mechanism associated with poverty, unemployment, and patriarchal and harmful social norms.

Oxfam conducted three sessions with young people and partners to define the advocacy priorities in 2022. Two main themes were identified: Youth access to comprehensive and correct SRH information, and women and girls with disabilities SRH rights. In 2023, a campaign strategy has been implemented to advocate for these priorities. The team worked on targeting laws and policies to adapt and/or improve to enable young people to enjoy their SRHR.

Masarouna partners aims at having one governmental policy adopted or improved during the course of the project, to enable diverse young people to claim their SRHR. During Year 2, partners will prioritize which policy will be specifically targeted for advocacy. This decision will be informed by the multiple studies currently conducted. The project aims at enhancing the referral and service provision targetting youth, enhance policy and service provision at government levels and enhance SRHR in relation topeople with disabilities (PWD) among others.

description.narrative: KI-1b # By-laws enabling diverse young people to enjoy their SRHR that are better implemented or enforced

comment.narrative: The National Health Strategy was adopted, which aims to ensure the provision of comprehensive and integrated services for all citizens. However, current health services provided are insufficient. The weak social system lacks integrated healthcare for women, despite the presence of women’s units in Ministries. In rural areas, effects stemming from the lack of services are magnified. Some communities receive irregular mobile clinic health services, forcing women to travel long distances to different towns and cities to access them.

The national SRHR strategy lacks inclusivity, specifically from a disability perspective. Therefore, one of the local partners of Oxfam conducted three meetings with the department of the Ministry of Health (MoH) in charge of women health, in order to discuss their interventions and possible ways to cooperate with the Ministry. The partner shared a proposed action plan for suggested interventions focused on inclusiveness for all (in particular people, including women and youth, living with disabilities),which was approved by the MoH department in charge of women health. A draft MoU was also shared with the Ministry of Health in June 2023, but no feedback received yet.

Masarouna partners aims at having one by-law better implemented during the course of the project, to enable diverse young people to claim their SRHR. During Year 2, partners will prioritize which by-law will be specifically targeted for advocacy. This decision will be informed by the multiple studies currently conducted. The project aims at enhancing the referral and service provision targetting youth, enhance policy and service provision at government levels and enhance SRHR in relation to people with disabilities (PWD) among others.

KI-9b # Governmental policies affecting NGOs, CSOs and/or labour/trade unions blocked, adopted and/or improved to improve civil society space

comment.narrative: Communities are subjected to violence, intimidation or repression, and authorities and non-state actors sponsor restrictions on the fundamental right of assembly and freedom of expression, especially targeting human rights defenders and their organisations who are key agents for resistance and change. While the occupation authorities continue to monitor and target civil society organizations and seek to dry-up their resources and restrict their movement and operations, the domestic authority has adopted practices to control and minimize the monitoring role of civil society organizations. A series of legislations threaten the existence of CSOs, especially the policy that was suggested by the government for the latter to give pre-approval for receiving funds. This suggested policy was challenged by CSOs and international donors and has not been put into effect until present, yet it comprises a threat and limitation on CSOs work. Another threat is the cybercrime law that gives the government the authority to monitor and block everything in the digital space.

Oxfam contracted a national NGO coalition as Masarouna partner in December 2022, so that they can collaborate on a campaign to target and address NGO and/or labour/trade union government policies that if adopted or improved, the civil society space will be enhanced. The NGO coalition released a social media campaign and statement in July 2023, addressing a policy that the Government is planning to implement which would be restricting the registration and sustainability of Non-profit organisations. All NGOs in the country are working towards stoping this restrictive policy from going into effect.

During Year 2, partners will prioritize which policy will be specifically targeted. This decision will be informed by a civic space workshop conducted with them. In 2023, the Oxfam Country Office will contract a local NGO coalition to work on blocking orbetter implementing policies that will improve the civic space work on NGOs.
Update Oct. 2023: Oxfam and partners are focusing on addressing a proposed government policy in the country that imposes limitations and threaten the sustainability of non-profit organizations. This policy imposes numerous restrictions on NGOs, requiring rigorous audit procedures, demands extensive involvement in program details, and establishes impractical requirements for registering new organizations. The partners are planning to launch a social media campaign and release statements opposing the policy and are collectively aiming to prevent the implementation of this restrictive policy and are actively working towards this goal. (The quantitative 5-year target remains thesame)

description.narrative: KI-9c # By-laws or codes of conducts affecting NGOs, CSOs and/or labour/trade unions that are better implemented or enforced to improve civil society space

comment.narrative: The growing discourse on security and countering terrorism grants the government and security apparatus a strong dominance on the work of CSOs. The occupation authorities' security apparatus controls agendas of CSOs and the type of activities they can conduct. The regulatory framework is complex given the different laws that apply in different areas of the country. A presidential decree regulates the work of CSOs forcing them to submit financial and operational plans at the beginning of the year. This requirement limits their work opportunities and reduces efficiency. Due to pressures by civil society and human rights actors as well as international actors the decree was cancelled for now by another presidential decree. However, it is unclear what might happen in the future. Moreover, certain regulations that apply on tendering and transfer of funds prohibits the transfer of funds, henceforth restricting the work and efficiency of civil society organizations.

Oxfam contracted a national NGO coalition as Masarouna partner in December 2022, so that they can work together on targeting NGO and/or labour/trade union by-laws or codes of conduct to improve civil society space to be better implemented or enforced.

During Year 2, partners will prioritize which by-law will be specifically targeted. This decision will be informed by a civic space workshop conducted with them. During Year 2, partners will prioritize which policy will be specifically targeted. This decision will be informed by a civic space workshop conducted with them. In 2023, the Oxfam Country Office will contract a local NGOs coalition to work on blocking or better implementing policies that will improve the civic space work on NGOs.
